source: RED-Green Belt Siem Reap network, facilitated with support from GIZ (German development cooperation) and Cambodian government partners, trifold brochure "វិធីដាំខ្នុរ" (How to Plant Jackfruit); practical training content credited to Ms. Chan Vin (អ្នកស្រី ចាន់វិន), a fruit-tree seedling vendor near Boeung Tonle Vil, Siem Reap; no publication date visible on the document.
text:
Seedlings need about 1 week of shade/hardening exposure before planting. Water the seedling 2 days before transplanting it into the pit.

Before planting, carefully remove the seedling from its planting bag/container. Peel the bag off gently, taking care not to disturb or break the root ball.

Place the seedling into the prepared pit, then backfill soil around it, pressing the soil down gently (not compacting it hard). Use a stake/stick tied to the young tree to support and stabilize it after planting.

Note: some phrases describing the exact bag-removal and staking technique in the source brochure were only partially legible; the general sequence above (shade-harden, pre-water, de-bag without breaking roots, backfill, gentle press, stake) is confident, but a few specific wording details could not be fully verified.
